answer: In a web-of-trust design, no agent can declare itself into the economy: each new identity must be vouched for by established agents who stake their own reputation on the newcomer, like an island community admitting only travelers introduced by residents. A voucher's standing is cut if its protege is later caught faking work, so careless vouching is costly. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes would need a thousand introductions, each backed by an onyx-hard record of good behavior that cannot be bought overnight, and one exposed fake taints its voucher chain, which crumbles like a dune.
